chunks: 3 - We were informed by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda, who said: Humeed ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Sabah, known as Ibn al-Dahhak, narrated to me, saying: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, from Ali (peace be upon him) that he said:

There will come to you after one hundred and fifty years, unbeliever rulers, untrusted treasurers, and dissolute officials. Then trade will increase but profits will decrease, usury will spread, illegitimate sons will become numerous, adultery will overwhelm, acquaintances will deny each other, the crescent moon will be regarded as greater than it is, a woman will be satisfied with a woman, and a man with a man.
A man narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that when he was reciting this hadith, a man stood up to him and said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, what shall we do in that time?

He said: Escape, escape! For the justice of Allah will still be spread over this ummah as long as their reciters (ulama) do not incline to their rulers, and as long as their pious do not forbid their dissolute. If they do not do so, and then they are alerted and say: There is no god but Allah, Allah will say from His Throne: You have lied; you are not truthful in it.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the later era and the advice of Imam Ali regarding governance and social decay?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ali (as) outlines the socio-political decay preceding the Mahdi's appearance, emphasizing that divine justice persists as long as the scholarly class (*qurra'*) and the pious (*abrar*) maintain independence from corrupt rulers. The advice to 'flee' (*al-harb*) signifies a strategic withdrawal from active political engagement during this era of widespread hypocrisy, where mere recitation of the Shahada becomes insufficient without genuine adherence. This highlights the Shia concept of *Taqiyya* and political quietism as a means of preserving faith until the emergence of the Just One.
